items.label: Listen, sing and move
src: Join in with the actions and invite the child to copy you. Keep this stage short and predictable so it works as a lesson-opening routine.
Ex 1.1 Listen, sing and move
Lead-in
Show the closed curtain.
Say, “Look! What’s behind the curtain? Let’s see!”
Do not ask the child to name the letters yet.
Point to each pair, model only the sound and invite the child to repeat: “/s/”, “/æ/”, “/t/”.
Support for less confident students:
Use a clear mouth position and a hand cue for each sound.
Let the child repeat together with you before saying the sound alone.
Fast finishers extension:
Point to the three letter pairs in a random order and let the child produce the sound without a model.

src: Point to the three letter pairs in a random order and let the child produce the sound without a model.
Ex 1.1 What's Behind the Curtain? Look, listen and say (gif)
Phonics song
Play the video once.
Ask the child only to watch and listen.
Before the second viewing, show the three movements: touch your ankle for sock, pretend to bite an apple, spin one finger like a top.
Play the video again and join in with the sounds, words and movements.
Pause after each target line if the child needs extra time.
Finish by pointing to S s, A a and T t and eliciting the sound.
Support for less confident students:
Pause after each letter scene. Say the sound together twice before continuing. The child can do the movement even if they are not ready to say the whole chant.
Fast finishers extension:
Mute the final repetition of each scene and let the child supply the sound and word.

parts.title: Look, trace and write (pic)
parts.html: Картинки нет — в исходнике не найдена, учитель добавит

Ученику скрыта

Letters

Show one letter pair at a time with numbered strokes and arrows.

Say, “Big S, little s”, then “Big A, little a”, then “Big T, little t”.

The child repeats the letter names.

Trace each model with your finger first.

Then complete the first trace together with the pen tool.

Support for less confident students:

Keep the stroke model visible. Let the child trace over a dotted letter before copying it into an empty space. Guide the first stroke verbally: “Start here. Down / round / across.”

Fast finishers extension:

After tracing, hide the stroke arrows and ask the child to write one uppercase and one lowercase letter from memory.

Ex 1.2 Match. Then say (pic)
Show Picture 1. Say, “Look carefully. Can you see a letter?”
Give the child time to look before helping.
Accept either the letter name or the sound.
Reveal or confirm the answer, then repeat with the other hidden letter shapes.
For the final minute, take turns making a letter shape with your body or hands.
The other person guesses the letter.
Support for less confident students:
Trace the hidden outline in the air or point to the beginning and end of the shape. Offer two choices: “S or T?”
Fast finishers extension:
Ask the child to make two different letter poses for you to guess, including one lowercase letter.

src: Children take turns making a pose. The rest of the group guesses together.
Ex 1.3 Look and say (pic)
Example:
Big **A**! Little **s**!
Point to the writing area and say, “Listen. Write the letter.”
Model the first item together. Say, “A.” Point to the Aa support in the corner and write A. Then call the remaining letters in a random order.
Alternate uppercase and lowercase explicitly by saying “Big S”, “little t”, etc.
At the end, point to each written letter and ask the child to name it.
Support for less confident students:
Keep Ss, Aa and Tt visible in the corner. If needed, let the child trace the support letter in the air before writing.
Fast finishers extension:
For the last two items, say only the sound rather than the letter name. The child decides which letter to write.

items.label: Chant! (audio + pic)
src: Play or model one line at a time. Ask the student to watch and copy you first. Then repeat the whole chant together.
Ex 1.4 Chant! (audio + pic)
Script
Sam, sand, nest Ann, hat, man Tom, tin, hat
Blending
Show the three lowercase letter tiles a-t.
Point to each tile and say the sound slowly: “/æ/ … /t/.”
The child repeats.
Then slide your finger from left to right under the tiles and blend: “/æ/— /t/ … at.”
Repeat twice, making the gaps shorter each time.
Do one blend together.
Then ask the child to slide their finger under the letters and blend independently.
